## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/drawer ``` The examples compose `@cadence/button`, `@cadence/field` and `@cadence/input` as needed. Install those items when copying their corresponding examples. **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines. | Item | Target file | Full source | | --- | --- | --- | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | drawer | `@components/cadence/drawer/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/drawer.json) | [Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) [Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) [Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) [Source files: drawer](https://cadence.dev/r/drawer.json) 4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once: ```tsx import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider"; export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return {children}; } ``` Copy all nine files in the target list, including every shared `lib/` file. Keep the mirrored `cadence/` tree, relative imports and `"use client"` directives intact. The popup and backdrop use CSS transitions, but the provider imports still require `motion`. The provider files are required; wrapping your application in `CadenceProvider` is optional. Complete the base theme setup linked above, including Cadence's easing tokens, and ensure Tailwind scans the copied files. There is no additional Drawer-specific CSS or asset in these payloads. Each portalled popup and backdrop resolves its own motion clock, including provider `timeScale`: full slides and fades the popup, reduced keeps the fade and drops the closed-state slide, and none removes authored transitions and hidden entry/exit opacity from the first frame. Direct finger tracking remains in all three modes. Without a wrapper, Drawer follows the system motion preference; a nested full scope still respects the system reduced-motion preference. Usage, the top Move conversation specimen and every body example additionally use [Button](/components/button). Controlled draft also needs [Field](/components/field) and [Input](/components/input). Install the items used by the example you copy: ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button @cadence/field @cadence/input ``` For manual installation, follow those pages' Manual tabs too. Button adds `button/index.tsx`; Controlled draft additionally adds `field/index.tsx`, `label/index.tsx`, `separator/index.tsx` and `input/index.tsx`. Reuse the shared files already listed here. Button and Field require this extra npm package; Input adds none beyond Drawer's complete dependency command: ```package-manager npm install class-variance-authority ``` Explicit motion scopes uses the included provider. The site's preview shell is not consumer setup. In Next.js App Router, Usage, the top Move conversation specimen, Snap points and Controlled draft need a client module for their state and event handlers. Use `alert-dialog`; a drawer can be dragged shut. - A hint on a control. Use `tooltip` or `hover-card`. - A long multi-step flow. Use a page or a `sheet` with a footer; dragging half-way through a form is a worse experience than a full surface. ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `Drawer` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal`, `snapPoints`, `swipeDirection`, `showSwipeHandle` | `showSwipeHandle` is additive; `swipeDirection` defaults to `"down"` and `modal` to `true`. | | `DrawerTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the drawer. | | `DrawerContent` | `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay (when modal), viewport, popup, and content. | | `DrawerOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `DrawerContent`. | | `DrawerSwipeHandle` | `className` | The handle; rendered for you when `showSwipeHandle` is set. | | `DrawerClose` | native button props, `render` | Closes the drawer. | | `DrawerHeader` / `DrawerFooter` | `className` | Stacking and spacing only. | | `DrawerTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. | | `DrawerDescription` | `className` | Supporting text. | ## Motion contract Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | enter | sheet `opacity 0 → 1` + `transform` from `--closed-transform`; backdrop `opacity 0 → 1` | `popup.anchored` · `duration.slow` / `duration.fast` | yes | | drag | `transform` follows `--drawer-swipe-movement-*`; backdrop opacity is `1 - --drawer-swipe-progress` | Base UI gesture (no authored recipe) | yes (it is the gesture) | | exit | sheet back to `--closed-transform` + `opacity → 0`; backdrop `opacity → 0` | `exit.fade` · `duration.slow` / `duration.fast` | yes | | reduced | fade only: the closed-state slide is dropped, so the sheet appears and disappears in place | `exit.fade` | yes | | none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the sheet is in place on the first frame | – | – | The drag keeps tracking the finger under `reduced`: that movement is the user's own, not authored motion, and a sheet that ignored the drag would be worse than one that follows it. The release animation uses the token duration rather than a velocity-scaled one — the swipe physics decide *where* the sheet settles, the token decides how long the settle takes. ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | --- | --- | | Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside a modal drawer. | | Escape | Closes the drawer and returns focus to the trigger. | | Enter / Space | Activates the focused control. | ## Accessibility - Base UI provides `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`, focus trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and Escape handling while the drawer is modal. - `DrawerTitle` is required: a drawer without an accessible name is invalid. - The swipe handle is `aria-hidden="true"` and is never the only way out. A user who cannot drag gets the close controls, Escape, and the overlay press (for a modal drawer). - The content region scrolls on its own (`overflow-y-auto`), so a long list inside the sheet does not move the page behind it. ## Responsive behavior The default sheet sits at the bottom, spans the width, and caps its height at `calc(100dvh - 3rem)` so a strip of the page stays visible. `swipeDirection="left"` / `"right"` becomes a side panel at `w-3/4`, capped at `max-w-sm` from `sm` up. Snap points change the resting height without changing any of that geometry. ## Performance - The drag writes CSS variables and a `transform`; it never touches layout or React state per frame. - The backdrop opacity is a `calc()` on the same variable, so the page behind dims as the sheet moves without a second animation. - Entry and exit animate `transform` and `opacity` only. Nothing is measured during render. ## Notes for AI - Use `drawer` for a short touch-first task from the bottom edge; use `sheet` for a side panel that holds a form, and `alert-dialog` when the answer must be deliberate. - Always render `DrawerTitle`. `DrawerDescription` is the second line of the announcement. - Never make the swipe the only dismissal: keep a `DrawerClose`, and let Escape work. - For a list of actions, each row is a `DrawerClose` so choosing one closes the sheet.
